items.summary: If the polls are right, Democrats will retake at least one chamber of Congress in the U.S. midterms. And with voters focused on the cost of living, foreign policy is an unusually impactful driver at the ballot box: Tariffs have raised the price of everyday goods, and the war with Iran has sent gas prices soaring. How might Democrats use their new power over spending and oversight to challenge Trump’s agenda in his final two years in office? How will allies and adversaries read the results? US forces have been restocking their munitions in the region, and bomber aircraft and jet fighters are preparing for attacks, officials told the WSJ. items.summary: Iran’s supreme leader directs judiciary to pursue US-Israeli war reparations Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has directed the judiciary to pursue compensation for "material and moral" damages caused by the US-Israeli war, state news agency IRNA reported. Khamenei issued the directive during a meeting with judiciary chief Gholam Hossein Mohseni Ejei, calling for the authorities to pursue the Iranian nation’s rights. He also urged the judiciary to step up its fight against corruption, address its underlying causes and accelerate the handling of cases, with timely enforcement of rulings to serve as a deterrent. items.title: Iran judiciary says chief holds rare meeting with supreme leader
items.summary: Iran judiciary says chief holds rare meeting with supreme leader Iran's judiciary said on Saturday that its chief held a rare meeting with the country's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who has yet to appear in public since being appointed. Mojtaba was chosen in March to succeed his father and longtime ruler Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in US-Israeli strikes in central Tehran alongside senior military commanders at the start of the Middle East war, and was said to have been injured in the same attack. Judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei and the supreme leader discussed issues including "securing public rights, and effectively combating corruption and its bottlenecks", the judiciary's Mizan Online website reported. They held talks on "pursuing the recovery of rights and compensation for material and moral damages arising from the crimes of American-Zionist criminals", it said.

items.summary: Iran's Bagheri confirms top officials from Mecca Pact countries' visit to Tehran The deputy secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, Ali Bagheri, announced the visit of senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey to Tehran. Bagheri said the meeting is aimed at discussing regional security, and will include Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani Army Commander General Asim Munir, and Turkish Intelligence Chief Ibrahim Kalin. "The Islamic Republic of Iran's model of defence based on internal and domestic capabilities has become a successful model for building national security," he said. "On the other hand, Iran's strategic policy is to ensure regional security through regional countries and confront any foreign interference and influence, led by the American and Zionist regimes." Bagheri described the initiative as the "fruit of the heroic efforts and struggles of the armed forces and the Iranian nation", expressing his hopes that it would lead to a "region with stability and peace and on the path of progress".

items.title: Israel’s Netanyahu clashes with army chief over Iran-related military action: Report
items.summary: Israel’s Netanyahu clashes with army chief over Iran-related military action: Report Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Army Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir reportedly had an "unprecedented confrontation" over a proposed military operation that could trigger a war with Iran ahead of the elections on Tuesday. According to Israeli Channel 12 reported Sunday, Zamir has resisted carrying out the military action - that remains unspecified - and requested signed documentation from Netanyahu regarding legal authorisation for it. "This relates to an action that could lead to a flare-up with Iran, at a sensitive and dramatic moment, creating this [potential] miscalculation," a military source was quoted as saying. The report also cited another source that said there is military concerns that the political leadership could exploit tensions with Iran for "political benefit". Channel 12 added that the hostility between Netanyahu and Zamir were evident at discussions on Sunday at the Palmahim Airbase, where the atmosphere in the room was described by a source as "extremely sour".

"We could end it very quickly," Trump said. "Do we want to finish it off or just want to let it wither?" Many rural homes have an open fire or wood burner, but most rely on kerosene oil for hot water and heating. Since the US-Iran war began, its cost has more than doubled. Currently, 1,000 litres (lasting 10-12 weeks) is £1,219. A year ago, it was £549. Seasoned wood is in demand. items.title: Piraten kapen Iraans schip bij Somalië, mogelijk met meer aanvallen als doel
items.summary: Somalische piraten hebben een Iraans vissersschip aangevallen en overmeesterd. Er zijn 23 bemanningsleden aan boord van het schip. Dat meldt de EU-missie die moet bijdragen aan de veiligheid op de West-Indische Oceaan en de Rode Zee. Het schip werd donderdag gekaapt ten noordoosten van Somalië, tussen de kustplaatsen Bandar Bayla en Hafun. Volgens het veiligheidscentrum zijn de piraten gewapend en is onduidelijk hoe de bemanning het maakt. De EU-missie waarschuwt dat het schip mogelijk als uitvalsbasis wordt gebruikt voor meer piraterij. Het nadert een commerciële scheepvaartroute, volgens de laatst bekende positie. Twaalf piraten Een medewerker van de maritieme politie van Puntland zegt tegen persbureau AP dat er twaalf piraten aan boord zijn gegaan van het Iraanse schip, de Azini. Op het schip waren 21 Iraniërs en twee Somalische beveiligers. De EU-missie onderzoekt het incident. Schepen in de buurt zijn opgeroepen alert te zijn op verdachte situaties en die onmiddellijk te melden. Meer kapingen De afgelopen maanden zijn er nog vijf piratenaanvallen geweest voor de kust van Somalië

items.summary: Iran submits evidence of US-Israeli attacks on maritime infrastructure to IMO Iran said it has submitted evidence of US and Israeli attacks on its maritime infrastructure to the International Maritime Organisation (IMO). The dossier of evidence given by Tehran to the IMO includes documents and photographic evidence of sabotage on its maritime infrastructure. An Iranian official said IMO member states will discuss the evidence at a council session taking place in London on 2-6 November. The attacks on its maritime infrastructure, according to Iran, threaten the safety of international shipping and seafarers. Iran's IRNA news agency reported that damage to maritime traffic control systems also increases the risk of accidents, and the destruction of rescue facilities undermines emergency response capabilities.

Israeli artillery also shelled Beit Yahoun, in the same district, and the area between the towns of Zawtar al-Sharqiya and Maifadoun. An Israeli air strike hit the town of Mansouri, while Israeli warplanes flew low over the city of Tyre and its surroundings, staging mock raids. Alongside ongoing demolitions, the Israeli army has been building several roads through mountains and valleys in the western and central parts of south Lebanon, connecting the military outposts it set up after occupying the area, according to NNA. Israel sharply escalated its military operations in Lebanon this year, launching a ground invasion and occupying large parts of the country’s south and east. items.summary: Van Alaska en Texas tot grote delen van het Amerikaanse midwesten; drie keer op rij wist Donald Trump er zonder al te veel moeite te winnen. Toch lijken dieprode Republikeinse staten nu Democratisch blauw te kunnen kleuren. In de laatste dagen voor de Congres-verkiezingen moeten Republikeinen alle zeilen bijzetten. "Dit zijn de cruciaalste verkiezingen van ons leven", zegt Ashley Hinson, Congreslid voor de Republikeinen. Ze hoopt een vrijkomende senaatszetel namens Iowa te claimen. Er is geen zekerheid: in de peilingen gaat ze nek aan nek met haar Democratische tegenkandidaat. "Wie heeft er al gestemd?" vraagt Hinson aan de mensen in een motelzaaltje in Coralville. Het merendeel van de vijftig aanwezigen steekt de hand omhoog. Op de meeste hier kan ze rekenen. Het motel ligt aan de I-80, de snelweg die de west- en oostkust van de VS met elkaar verbindt. New York en San Francisco, het begin- en eindpunt van de snelweg, zijn blauw: daar wordt steevast Democratisch gestemd. items.summary: Iran could revisit nuclear weapons ban if war resumes, security chief says Iran is debating whether to maintain its longstanding ban on nuclear weapons if hostilities resume, though no decision has been taken on any change, Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei told state media on Saturday. Rezaei also said Washington's tone had shifted as it sought to restart negotiations with the Islamic Republic. The US Vice President JD Vance wrote to Rezaei last week in a bid to revive diplomacy. According to the New York Times, Qatari mediators handed the letter to Rezaei. It proposed direct talks headed by Vance, with Iran's nuclear programme up for discussion from the outset. "I read the letter. I haven’t yet responded. Their tone has completely changed," Rezaei said, calling the shift "a good sign" that showed Iran had "consolidated its victory". He declined to comment further on the letter's contents, but said Iran's nuclear issue could be discussed only after the United States met Iran's demands. items.title: Khamenei orders immediate response to any threat 'without geographical limitations'
items.summary: Khamenei orders immediate response to any threat 'without geographical limitations' Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered the country’s armed forces to deliver an "immediate, effective response without geographical limitations" to any potential enemy threat, according to the state news agency IRNA. In directives issued after a meeting with senior military commanders, Khamenei called for “intelligent combat readiness” to ensure what he described as “maximum deterrence”. He also ordered an update to Iran’s “Targets Bank” to bring tangible and intangible US and Israeli assets within the reach of Iranian forces. Khamenei further called for strengthening Iran’s military information systems, developing domestic defence capabilities and incorporating new technologies into its security and military infrastructure. “If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for their end,” he said.

As the 2026 midterm elections approach, divisions within the MAGA camp are becoming increasingly visible. From the war in Iran and rising fuel prices to the Epstein files, several of Trump’s decisions are fuelling divisions among his most loyal supporters.
 
Once united by a shared vision of America, MAGA now brings together factions that increasingly disagree over foreign policy, the economy and what “America First” should actually mean. Yet Trump remains the central figure holding this political coalition together – and he is fighting to keep it that way.
 
Why are some of the president’s longtime allies distancing themselves from him? Can MAGA remain united despite these disagreements? And can Trump still mobilise his base ahead of the midterms?
 
🔍 Our journalist Stella Elgersma breaks down the divisions within the MAGA movement and Donald Trump’s strategy to rally his supporters, once again.

The first spill to reach the coast left dark slicks along beaches, with authorities closing affected areas in Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah. The UAE environment ministry said it was coordinating cleanup operations and urged fishermen to avoid polluted areas. Marine monitor Windward recorded 12 spills between July and September, including one that spread across an area of 2,000 square kilometres off Oman. Satellite imagery also showed an oil slick near Ras Al Khaimah. Experts warned that turtles, dolphins, seabirds and other marine species could be affected. items.summary: Palestinian journalist returns home after 15 months in Israeli detention Palestinian journalist Farah Abu Ayyash has returned home to her family following 450 days of detention in Israeli prisons, according to a report by the Islamic Republic News Agency (Irna). Abu Ayyash, a West Bank correspondent for Iran's Tasnim News Agency, was freed on Thursday night after the Ofer Prison military court ordered her release, dismissing the charges brought against her after she served 15 months under administrative detention. According to Irna, Abu Ayyash was initially detained on 6 August 2025, during an overnight military raid on her family home in Beit Ummar, north of Hebron. The outlet reported that her arrest was tied to her journalistic work covering local developments across the southern West Bank for Tasnim. The report further noted that repeated procedural delays prolonged her case, keeping her detained without formal resolution under administrative detention at Damon Prison. Irna also reported that the correspondent was allegedly subjected to torture and mistreatment while in custody.

items.summary: Iran slams Canada for supporting UAE claim over three Gulf islands Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei has criticised Canada's support for the United Arab Emirates' claim to three Gulf islands, questioning Ottawa's commitment to territorial integrity and national sovereignty. In a post on X, Baqaei said the UAE, established in 1971, was laying claim to Abu Musa and the Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb despite "historical records and geographical and documented evidence establishing their Iranian ownership". He said the islands had been part of Iran for millennia, long before the UAE federation was established, and criticised Canada's prime minister for echoing what he called an “absurd claim”. Baqaei invoked Canada's own history of defending its sovereignty, citing the American invasion during the War of 1812, the Montreal Annexation Manifesto of 1849 and US President Donald Trump's repeated remarks about making Canada the 51st US state. “How can it take sides in a fabricated dispute and endorse an unfounded territorial claim that amounts to dangerous adventurism?” he said.

Muscat’s navy “carried out an evacuation operation for 25 crew members of the merchant ship Riti, flying the Panamanian flag, after it was targeted, which led to a fire breaking out on board”, Oman’s Maritime Security Centre said in a statement. The crew members were provided with medical care, the Omani statement said. The MarineTraffic ship-tracking website described the Riti as a crude oil tanker. In a video released earlier on Friday, Centcom chief Brad Cooper said US forces had “successfully cleared the strait’s internationally recognised primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines”. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps said separately that three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified “incidents” or hitting mines.

items.summary: Centcom chief says Hormuz routes remain clear as Iran reports interceptions The head of US Central Command (Centcom), Admiral Brad Cooper, has claimed that the main international shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz are clear of Iranian sea mines and that commercial vessels are sailing freely through the waterway. In a video posted on Cencom's X account, Cooper said he flew over the strait earlier this week and saw dozens of commercial vessels transiting the area. “Here’s what I didn’t see: I didn’t see the IRGC out there at all,” he said, claiming Iran’s navy was “all at the bottom of the sea”. The remarks come as Iran has repeatedly claimed that it maintains control over the strait. Earlier, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had stopped two tankers attempting to cross the southern part of the waterway, accusing them of using “unauthorised routes” with US military support.

clusters.headline: Old News: After 26-year rule, Shah of Iran crowns himself ‘King of Kings’

items.title: Old News: After 26-year rule, Shah of Iran crowns himself ‘King of Kings’
items.summary: Old News is a new initiative by Amwaj.media to connect the past to the present. Through “reporting” on pivotal moments in history, we aim to provide a richer backdrop for current dynamics in the region. The story: Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi has crowned himself Iran’s “King of Kings,” and his wife as Empress. The event took place at a lavish ceremony in Tehran's Golestan Palace, 26 years after becoming head of state. Observers say Pahlavi has delayed his coronation to await the birth of a male heir, and to initiate enough progress and reform in Iran to legitimize his rule. The coronation has drawn national and international praise for reforms implemented as part of the Shah’s “White Revolution,” though he is also facing domestic criticism for his policies and autocratic rule. The coverage: Pahlavi crowned himself Shahanshah , “King of Kings” of the Imperial State of Iran, on Oct. 26 1967—marking his 48th birthday.

clusters.headline: Vast, variabel of dynamisch? Huishoudens op zoek naar juiste energiecontract

items.title: Vast, variabel of dynamisch? Huishoudens op zoek naar juiste energiecontract
items.summary: Al maanden stijgen de prijzen voor olie en gas door de oorlog in het Midden-Oosten. Grote energieconcerns lijden daar niet onder, blijkt vandaag uit cijfers. Terwijl de bedrijven hoge winsten behalen, blijven de energietarieven voor consumenten alsmaar oplopen. En dat levert de vraag op: kun je het beste een vast, variabel of toch dynamisch contract afsluiten? Verschillende energiebedrijven maakten de torenhoge winsten bekend die ze de afgelopen drie maanden hebben gemaakt. Zo zagen Shell en Vattenfall hun winst verdubbelen door de hoge olie- en gasprijs. Ondertussen kwam de gasprijs voor een megawattuur gisteren voor het eerst sinds het najaar van 2022 boven de 100 euro uit. De stijgende gasrekening leidt tot vragen bij de Consumentenbond. "Heel veel vragen van mensen over wat ze moeten doen. Het leeft ontzettend", zegt Joyce Donat van de Consumentenbond. Ook consumentencollectief United Consumers ziet dat klanten op zoek zijn naar antwoorden en zekerheid. Toch is er geen pasklaar antwoord. Vast contract "Tot voor kort loonde het om een vast contract af te sluiten net voor de zomer.

The proposal — the latest in a series of recent Russian offers to act as an intermediary between Washington and Tehran — has a certain logic to it. While the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran has brought Russia some economic gains through rising energy prices, Moscow fears further escalation and spillover across the Persian Gulf and parts of the former Soviet space. Russia is also one of Iran’s closest partners and one of the world’s leading exporters of enriched uranium, meaning that it could help break the impasse over domestic Iranian nuclear enrichment. Yet Moscow will struggle to gain Western and Gulf Arab acceptance as a mediator, particularly amid the Ukraine conflict and heightened threat perceptions of Iran in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) while Russia is increasingly aligned with Iran. clusters.headline: Labour is still searching for an energy fix for a new world

items.title: Labour is still searching for an energy fix for a new world
items.summary: The chancellor is right to focus on pure affordability, but £100 handouts and delayed decisions won’t shield consumers from the next wave of price hikes Amid the myriad of small measures, virtually everything in John Healey’s budget came back to the cost of energy. The higher energy prices that have resulted from the Iran war have pushed up inflation, are eating into households’ incomes, are a drag on businesses – and are the main reason why the forecast for GDP growth next year was cut from 1.6% to just 1%. And energy was the focus of Healey’s sole surprise in his consumer-facing policies – the £100 payment to 20m households in A-D council tax bands to help with fuel bills this winter. It will be funded, in effect, by tapping the banks for a few quid for 15 months via the bank surcharge. Continue reading...

items.title: The Guardian view on Israel’s elections: Netanyahu lost his mandate. If opponents unite, he’ll lose power too | Editorial
items.summary: His chief rival should reject the prime minister’s anti-democratic vision and work with Palestinian Israeli parties Benjamin Netanyahu has lost his mandate but not, so far, power. While final votes are still being tallied, most voters picked his opponents on Tuesday. His bloc’s share of seats remains the largest, but appears to have slumped by around 10, leaving it below the 61 needed for a majority in the Knesset. Palestinian Israeli parties surged, and are projected to almost double the 10 seats they held. The result is that Mr Netanyahu’s main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot, a former head of the military, now faces a choice: fall into line with Mr Netanyahu’s racist fearmongering or work with Arab-led parties. While the pressure failed to defeat the measure, it created a notable shift in the vote tally. clusters.headline: The Legacy of Reykjavik and the Future of U.S.–Russia Nuclear Relations

items.title: The Legacy of Reykjavik and the Future of U.S.–Russia Nuclear Relations
items.summary: On 11-12 October 1986, U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev met in Reykjavik, Iceland, hoping to achieve a groundbreaking agreement on controlling the world’s most dangerous weapons. While the summit yielded no agreement, it set in motion arms control negotiations tracks, held up the promise of nuclear disarmament, and contributed to the transformation of relations between two Cold War ach-adversaries. Forty years on, what lessons does Reykjavik hold for arms control, disarmament, and great power relations? To discuss the legacy of Reykjavik, Project on Managing the Atom (MTA) is honored to welcome Pavel Palazhchenko, former interpreter of Mikhail Gorbachev and an ambassador of the Gorbachev Foundation, David Holloway, Professor Emeritus of Stanford University and author of the International History of Nuclear Weapons, Matthew Bunn, Professor at Harvard Kennedy School, and Carol Saivetz, Senior Fellow at MIT Security Studies Program, with Mariana Budjeryn, MTA associate and a senior researcher at MIT as moderator.

items.summary: There was a time when Europe was serious about diplomacy — diplomacy as the patient, often frustrating business of engaging adversaries, rather than merely issuing condemnations and imposing sanctions. Over and over, Kyiv and its backers have issued urgent demands for a new weapon or capability billed as the key to turning the tide of the war in Ukraine’s favor. Each time, after protesting, the U.S. chose to give in. And each time, the promised silver bullet failed to solve Kyiv’s battlefield challenges. Now, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky and his champions in the U.S. Congress are back with their next request: the intelligence, targeting support , and weapons to find and destroy Russian ballistic missile launchers inside of Russia. As in previous instances, the plan is described as foolproof, an “ easy ” fix for Ukraine’s air defense challenge, and nearly costless for American taxpayers. clusters.headline: Iran Nuclear Deal Implementation Day: A Belfer Center Expert Round-Up

items.title: Iran Nuclear Deal Implementation Day: A Belfer Center Expert Round-Up
items.summary: The Iran nuclear deal was officially implemented on Saturday, as Iran successfully fulfilled its initial key nuclear commitments and the international community relieved major sanctions, including unfreezing about $100 billion of Iranian money. Implementation Day was met with applause from deal supporters in the U.S. and Iran, while critics have raised questions about whether Iran will adhere to its requirements and how it will flex its newfound economic power. Also in recent days, the U.S. and Iran agreed to a prisoner swap that led to the freedom of Washington Post reporter Jason Rezaian and others, and negotiated the release of American sailors detained in Iran. What does the arrival of Implementation Day mean for Iran’s nuclear program and nuclear nonproliferation, and how does it bode for the future of U.S.-Iran relations? We asked Belfer Center experts to weigh in on these and related questions.

clusters.headline: Belfer Center Insights into Paris Attacks

items.title: Belfer Center Insights into Paris Attacks
items.summary: The terrorist attacks in Paris on November 13, which killed at least 129 people and injured hundreds of others, stunned the international community. In the days since, there has been renewed debate over a host of issues, including the strategy to defeat ISIS, the Syrian migrant crisis, and where the terrorist group might strike next. The attacks have also intensified the diplomacy surrounding the Syrian Civil War, and reopened the debate over the proper balance between security and privacy in the Western world. Belfer Center experts have been weighing in on these and related topics. See our guide to their thoughts and insights.

Mostafavi – who documented his ascents of some of the world’s highest peaks, including Mount Everest – was executed on 14 October having been arrested in April after the anti-government protests a few months earlier. His death followed the killing of Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi, a taekwondo athlete, at the start of October, and the mixed martial arts fighter Gholamreza Khani Shakarab, who was hanged in May. items.summary: Iran's supreme leader: A strong Iran rests upon scientific power In a statement shared by Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Monday, Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei emphasised the importance of scientific progress to Iran's strength. "The key to making Iran even stronger is the boundary-breaking work and problem-solving of the country's elites in scientific matters," Khamenei said in the statement addressed to Iranian elites and scientific and sporting medalists competing internationally. "The malice and crimes committed by the enemies of Islamic Iran against its scientists and elites demonstrate the effective role of elites in strengthening the country," Khamenei added, calling on officials to "provide necessary infrastructure" for a deep and rapid scientific leap. The statement was read at a ceremony honouring Iranian scientific and sports medalists, Tasnim reported.

items.summary: KLM vliegt de hele winter niet meer op Dubai, de grootste stad van de Arabische Emiraten. Dit is besloten omdat de situatie in het Midden-Oosten op dit moment onvoorspelbaar is, zegt een woordvoerder. Om dezelfde reden zijn de vluchten op de luchthavens van Dammam en Riyad in Saudi-Arabië opgeschort tot 27 november. Na de Amerikaanse en Israëlische aanvallen op Iran in het voorjaar is het in de landen rond de Perzische Golf nooit rustig geweest. Iran blokkeert de doorvaart door de zeestraat en bestookt landen in de regio met raketten en drones. Houthi's uit Jemen vielen deze maand vliegvelden in Saudi-Arabië aan. Vorige week groeide de vrees voor nieuwe grootschalige Amerikaanse en Israëlische aanvallen op Iran en voor de reactie van Iran daarop. In verband met de oorlogshandelingen in het gebied vliegt KLM al bijna het hele jaar niet op Dammam, Riyad en Dubai. Het besluit om het niet vliegen op Dubai te verlengen tot het voorjaar (27 maart) vloeit voort uit een combinatie van factoren, zegt de woordvoerder. items.title: The anti-China coalition is breaking apart at the seams
items.summary: Arriving in the White House in 2021, President Joe Biden set about dismantling much of his predecessor’s foreign-policy agenda. But there was one clear area of continuity: China. Here, Biden retained the first Trump administration’s confrontational approach, expanding the use of export controls on advanced technology and keeping China as the U.S. military’s pacing threat . In a time of deep political division, the newly formed China consensus appeared all-powerful. When the House voted in January 2023 to establish a select committee on “Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party,” the tally was 365 to 65. Once President Donald Trump returned to power, observers expected more of the same. But Trump has instead moved U.S. China policy in the opposite direction, seeking to de-escalate bilateral tension in favor of “ constructive strategic stability ” and revealing that the bipartisan consensus on the “China threat” may be more ephemeral than many assumed. items.summary: La visita triunfal de Felipe VI a Ceuta y Melilla es muy reveladora de la naturaleza de la monarquía en comparación con los demás regímenes políticos. Es imposible imaginar a ningún jefe de Gobierno español –ni de ningún otro país– aclamado durante una visita semejante. La explicación es sencilla: el Rey encarna a España , es España más allá de todas las divisiones partidistas. Solo un monarca, si su reinado es digno, puede encarnar así a toda una nación en un clima de unanimidad. Pero una monarquía no se improvisa; solo es legítima en la medida en que se inscribe en una larga historia. España tiene ese privilegio, al igual que los países escandinavos y Gran Bretaña. Pero la idea de la monarquía está lejos de ser estrictamente local, ni está anclada en el pasado, ni es arcaica. items.title: Libris Geschiedenis Prijs 2026 naar Maite Karssenberg voor boek Dubbelleven
items.summary: Schrijver Maite Karssenberg krijgt de Libris Geschiedenis Prijs voor haar biografie Dubbelleven. Geertruida Kapteyn-Muysken en haar rebelse levensfilosofie. De prijs voor het beste geschiedenisboek van het jaar werd uitgereikt door juryvoorzitter Frits Spits in een speciale uitzending van het VPRO-radioprogramma OVT. Karssenberg krijgt 20.000 euro. 'Schrikbarend ondergeschikt' Het boek legt de "schrikbarend ondergeschikte rol van de vrouw in de 19e eeuw bloot", zegt de jury. Geertruida Kapteyn-Muysken leefde van 1855 tot 1920. Ze filosofeerde over een betere wereld, maar was tegelijkertijd een getrouwde vrouw met kinderen die het huishouden moest doen. De hoofdpersoon wilde studeren en de wereld verbeteren, maar moest vechten voor haar kansen. Uiteindelijk kwam ze bij een internationale groep idealisten, feministen en anarchisten en hervond ze zichzelf. Wat de jury vooral boeiend vindt aan het boek is de "volstrekt originele manier" waarop Karssenberg de biografie heeft vormgegeven, zegt Spits. Barack Obama torna in prima linea nella campagna per le elezioni di metà mandato del 3 novembre. Dal palco di Cleveland, dove sostiene i democratici Sherrod Brown per il Senato e Amy Acton per la guida dell’Ohio, l’ex presidente attribuisce direttamente all’amministrazione Trump l’aumento del costo della vita. clusters.headline: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield

items.title: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield
items.summary: We’ve heard much about the end of the west. At the proposed summit between Trump, Putin and Xi, those fears could crystallise In the final two years of a US presidency, when Congress has been lost, approval ratings have sunk like a stone and their party has started to think about who’s coming next, the person occupying the Oval Office can feel their power draining away. Domestic legislation, particularly in an era where bipartisan cooperation is almost nonexistent, grinds to a halt. But as the days tick by until the end, and as presidents begin to think about their legacy, there is one part of the job where they still have power: the rest of the world. In the final weeks of his presidency in 1992 George HW Bush sent 28,000 American troops to Somalia to help end a famine. For Bill Clinton, it was a quixotic attempt to bring peace to the Middle East by ending the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Barack Obama restored diplomatic ties with Cuba, making a historic visit to Havana, as well as a final, successful push on the Iran nuclear deal. Continue reading...

items.title: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes
items.summary: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes Iran warned on Sunday that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to "take care" of more targets. Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the US and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections. "A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion," said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television. Akraminia's remarks followed Trump's suggestion that the US could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran.

items.title: Piraten kapen Iraans schip bij Somalië, mogelijk met meer aanvallen als doel
items.summary: Somalische piraten hebben een Iraans vissersschip aangevallen en overmeesterd. Er zijn 23 bemanningsleden aan boord van het schip. Dat meldt de EU-missie die moet bijdragen aan de veiligheid op de West-Indische Oceaan en de Rode Zee. Het schip werd donderdag gekaapt ten noordoosten van Somalië, tussen de kustplaatsen Bandar Bayla en Hafun. Volgens het veiligheidscentrum zijn de piraten gewapend en is onduidelijk hoe de bemanning het maakt. De EU-missie waarschuwt dat het schip mogelijk als uitvalsbasis wordt gebruikt voor meer piraterij. Het nadert een commerciële scheepvaartroute, volgens de laatst bekende positie. Twaalf piraten Een medewerker van de maritieme politie van Puntland zegt tegen persbureau AP dat er twaalf piraten aan boord zijn gegaan van het Iraanse schip, de Azini. Op het schip waren 21 Iraniërs en twee Somalische beveiligers. De EU-missie onderzoekt het incident. Schepen in de buurt zijn opgeroepen alert te zijn op verdachte situaties en die onmiddellijk te melden. Meer kapingen De afgelopen maanden zijn er nog vijf piratenaanvallen geweest voor de kust van Somalië

items.title: Houthis repeat threats against Saudi oil giant, aviation
items.summary: Houthis repeat threats against Saudi oil giant, aviation Houthi media, citing an anonymous military official, on Sunday repeated threats against Saudi oil giant Aramco and aviation in the kingdom. Yemen's Houthis, fighting a Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government, are allies of Iran, which on Sunday warned the US and Israel not to renew strikes on the Islamic Republic after they had threatened a return to war. "Aramco facilities are within range of the Yemeni Armed Forces, and investments in them are a venture fraught with losses," the Houthis' Saba news agency quoted the military official as saying. The official also warned international airlines against using Saudi airspace "except for the airspaces of Mecca and Medina".

An Iranian official said IMO member states will discuss the evidence at a council session taking place in London on 2-6 November. items.title: Khamenei orders immediate response to any threat 'without geographical limitations'
items.summary: Khamenei orders immediate response to any threat 'without geographical limitations' Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered the country’s armed forces to deliver an "immediate, effective response without geographical limitations" to any potential enemy threat, according to the state news agency IRNA. In directives issued after a meeting with senior military commanders, Khamenei called for “intelligent combat readiness” to ensure what he described as “maximum deterrence”. He also ordered an update to Iran’s “Targets Bank” to bring tangible and intangible US and Israeli assets within the reach of Iranian forces. Khamenei further called for strengthening Iran’s military information systems, developing domestic defence capabilities and incorporating new technologies into its security and military infrastructure. “If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for their end,” he said.

The first spill to reach the coast left dark slicks along beaches, with authorities closing affected areas in Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah. The UAE environment ministry said it was coordinating cleanup operations and urged fishermen to avoid polluted areas. Marine monitor Windward recorded 12 spills between July and September, including one that spread across an area of 2,000 square kilometres off Oman. Satellite imagery also showed an oil slick near Ras Al Khaimah. Experts warned that turtles, dolphins, seabirds and other marine species could be affected. Authorities have not identified the leaking vessel, but marine security experts cited by the FT said it was the Chinese-owned supertanker Gem No. 2, hit off Sharjah more than two weeks ago. items.title: Palestinian journalist returns home after 15 months in Israeli detention
items.summary: Palestinian journalist returns home after 15 months in Israeli detention Palestinian journalist Farah Abu Ayyash has returned home to her family following 450 days of detention in Israeli prisons, according to a report by the Islamic Republic News Agency (Irna). Abu Ayyash, a West Bank correspondent for Iran's Tasnim News Agency, was freed on Thursday night after the Ofer Prison military court ordered her release, dismissing the charges brought against her after she served 15 months under administrative detention. According to Irna, Abu Ayyash was initially detained on 6 August 2025, during an overnight military raid on her family home in Beit Ummar, north of Hebron. The outlet reported that her arrest was tied to her journalistic work covering local developments across the southern West Bank for Tasnim. The report further noted that repeated procedural delays prolonged her case, keeping her detained without formal resolution under administrative detention at Damon Prison. Irna also reported that the correspondent was allegedly subjected to torture and mistreatment while in custody.

Muscat’s navy “carried out an evacuation operation for 25 crew members of the merchant ship Riti, flying the Panamanian flag, after it was targeted, which led to a fire breaking out on board”, Oman’s Maritime Security Centre said in a statement. The crew members were provided with medical care, the Omani statement said. The MarineTraffic ship-tracking website described the Riti as a crude oil tanker. In a video released earlier on Friday, Centcom chief Brad Cooper said US forces had “successfully cleared the strait’s internationally recognised primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines”. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps said separately that three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified “incidents” or hitting mines.

The remarks come as Iran has repeatedly claimed that it maintains control over the strait. items.title: Old News: After 26-year rule, Shah of Iran crowns himself ‘King of Kings’
items.summary: Old News is a new initiative by Amwaj.media to connect the past to the present. Through “reporting” on pivotal moments in history, we aim to provide a richer backdrop for current dynamics in the region. The story: Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi has crowned himself Iran’s “King of Kings,” and his wife as Empress. The event took place at a lavish ceremony in Tehran's Golestan Palace, 26 years after becoming head of state. Observers say Pahlavi has delayed his coronation to await the birth of a male heir, and to initiate enough progress and reform in Iran to legitimize his rule. The coronation has drawn national and international praise for reforms implemented as part of the Shah’s “White Revolution,” though he is also facing domestic criticism for his policies and autocratic rule. The coverage: Pahlavi crowned himself Shahanshah , “King of Kings” of the Imperial State of Iran, on Oct. 26 1967—marking his 48th birthday.

items.title: The Legacy of Reykjavik and the Future of U.S.–Russia Nuclear Relations
items.summary: On 11-12 October 1986, U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev met in Reykjavik, Iceland, hoping to achieve a groundbreaking agreement on controlling the world’s most dangerous weapons. While the summit yielded no agreement, it set in motion arms control negotiations tracks, held up the promise of nuclear disarmament, and contributed to the transformation of relations between two Cold War ach-adversaries. Forty years on, what lessons does Reykjavik hold for arms control, disarmament, and great power relations? To discuss the legacy of Reykjavik, Project on Managing the Atom (MTA) is honored to welcome Pavel Palazhchenko, former interpreter of Mikhail Gorbachev and an ambassador of the Gorbachev Foundation, David Holloway, Professor Emeritus of Stanford University and author of the International History of Nuclear Weapons, Matthew Bunn, Professor at Harvard Kennedy School, and Carol Saivetz, Senior Fellow at MIT Security Studies Program, with Mariana Budjeryn, MTA associate and a senior researcher at MIT as moderator.

items.summary: There was a time when Europe was serious about diplomacy — diplomacy as the patient, often frustrating business of engaging adversaries, rather than merely issuing condemnations and imposing sanctions. In the wake of the October 7 attacks, regional tensions with Iran, and deepening domestic divisions, Greilsammer argues that the election will be fundamentally shaped by concerns over democratic accountability, judicial independence and the unequal distribution of civic obligations. He warns Netanyahu’s policies risk transforming Israel into “something like an authoritarian or non-democratic state.” He suggests that Israel’s Arab political parties could play a decisive role in determining the election’s outcome.

items.title: Iran Nuclear Deal Implementation Day: A Belfer Center Expert Round-Up
items.summary: The Iran nuclear deal was officially implemented on Saturday, as Iran successfully fulfilled its initial key nuclear commitments and the international community relieved major sanctions, including unfreezing about $100 billion of Iranian money. Implementation Day was met with applause from deal supporters in the U.S. and Iran, while critics have raised questions about whether Iran will adhere to its requirements and how it will flex its newfound economic power. Also in recent days, the U.S. and Iran agreed to a prisoner swap that led to the freedom of Washington Post reporter Jason Rezaian and others, and negotiated the release of American sailors detained in Iran. What does the arrival of Implementation Day mean for Iran’s nuclear program and nuclear nonproliferation, and how does it bode for the future of U.S.-Iran relations? We asked Belfer Center experts to weigh in on these and related questions.

items.title: Belfer Center Insights into Paris Attacks
items.summary: The terrorist attacks in Paris on November 13, which killed at least 129 people and injured hundreds of others, stunned the international community. In the days since, there has been renewed debate over a host of issues, including the strategy to defeat ISIS, the Syrian migrant crisis, and where the terrorist group might strike next. The attacks have also intensified the diplomacy surrounding the Syrian Civil War, and reopened the debate over the proper balance between security and privacy in the Western world. Belfer Center experts have been weighing in on these and related topics. See our guide to their thoughts and insights.

For the Islamic Republic, the meeting is a public relations victory, already presented as proof that the region can manage its own security. Saudi Arabia calls it an effort to de-escalate. Es imposible imaginar a ningún jefe de Gobierno español –ni de ningún otro país– aclamado durante una visita semejante. La explicación es sencilla: el Rey encarna a España , es España más allá de todas las divisiones partidistas. Solo un monarca, si su reinado es digno, puede encarnar así a toda una nación en un clima de unanimidad. Pero una monarquía no se improvisa; solo es legítima en la medida en que se inscribe en una larga historia. España tiene ese privilegio, al igual que los países escandinavos y Gran Bretaña. items.summary: Schrijver Maite Karssenberg krijgt de Libris Geschiedenis Prijs voor haar biografie Dubbelleven. Geertruida Kapteyn-Muysken en haar rebelse levensfilosofie. De prijs voor het beste geschiedenisboek van het jaar werd uitgereikt door juryvoorzitter Frits Spits in een speciale uitzending van het VPRO-radioprogramma OVT. Karssenberg krijgt 20.000 euro. 'Schrikbarend ondergeschikt' Het boek legt de "schrikbarend ondergeschikte rol van de vrouw in de 19e eeuw bloot", zegt de jury. Geertruida Kapteyn-Muysken leefde van 1855 tot 1920. Ze filosofeerde over een betere wereld, maar was tegelijkertijd een getrouwde vrouw met kinderen die het huishouden moest doen. De hoofdpersoon wilde studeren en de wereld verbeteren, maar moest vechten voor haar kansen. Uiteindelijk kwam ze bij een internationale groep idealisten, feministen en anarchisten en hervond ze zichzelf. Wat de jury vooral boeiend vindt aan het boek is de "volstrekt originele manier" waarop Karssenberg de biografie heeft vormgegeven, zegt Spits. items.summary: Iran judiciary says chief holds rare meeting with supreme leader Iran's judiciary said on Saturday that its chief held a rare meeting with the country's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who has yet to appear in public since being appointed. Mojtaba was chosen in March to succeed his father and longtime ruler Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in US-Israeli strikes in central Tehran alongside senior military commanders at the start of the Middle East war, and was said to have been injured in the same attack. Judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei and the supreme leader discussed issues including "securing public rights, and effectively combating corruption and its bottlenecks", the judiciary's Mizan Online website reported. They held talks on "pursuing the recovery of rights and compensation for material and moral damages arising from the crimes of American-Zionist criminals", it said.

items.title: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield
items.summary: We’ve heard much about the end of the west. At the proposed summit between Trump, Putin and Xi, those fears could crystallise In the final two years of a US presidency, when Congress has been lost, approval ratings have sunk like a stone and their party has started to think about who’s coming next, the person occupying the Oval Office can feel their power draining away. Domestic legislation, particularly in an era where bipartisan cooperation is almost nonexistent, grinds to a halt. But as the days tick by until the end, and as presidents begin to think about their legacy, there is one part of the job where they still have power: the rest of the world. In the final weeks of his presidency in 1992 George HW Bush sent 28,000 American troops to Somalia to help end a famine. For Bill Clinton, it was a quixotic attempt to bring peace to the Middle East by ending the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Barack Obama restored diplomatic ties with Cuba, making a historic visit to Havana, as well as a final, successful push on the Iran nuclear deal. Continue reading...

items.summary: Israelis head to the polls on October 27 in a vote that will cast Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing and religious allies against a motley crew of opposition parties. At the moment, neither side is expected to have a clear path to the 61-seat majority needed to form a government in the 120-seat Knesset. Netanyahu and his leading opponent are only projected to win some 20 seats each, but the biggest party doesn’t necessarily get the right to form the government. Instead, the Israeli president hands that job to whichever Knesset member has the best shot at winning the Knesset’s confidence. Tuesday’s vote should offer an early indication of which candidate will earn that right. While both main parties in contention advocate continued wars against Hamas and Iran, they differ on key domestic issues as well as their approach to settler violence in the West Bank. The source told Fars agency that if oil smuggling resumes, IRGC's response will be "far more forceful". items.title: Turkey warns against renewed attack on Iran, says diplomacy only way
items.summary: Turkey warns against renewed attack on Iran, says diplomacy only way Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan cautioned on Friday against any renewed attack on Iran, saying such a move would exacerbate tensions and further expand the conflict. Diplomacy and dialogue are the only way to end the war, Fidan told the press after meeting with foreign ministers from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Germany, France, Britain and Italy. "A military intervention on Iran is not in any way a solution. Nobody approves this at the moment," he added. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot also said after Friday's meetings that renewed escalation between Iran and the United States would only have losers and raise oil prices. items.title: Iran has plans to target Gulf undersea cables if attacked again, officials say
items.summary: Iran has plans to target Gulf undersea cables if attacked again, officials say Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack Iran again, two senior Iranian security officials told Reuters. Speaking on condition of anonymity, the officials gave few details and did not say how or where Tehran would carry out such attacks. But one of them said Iran would aim to prevent repairs after any attacks to prolong disruptions to communications, including internet connections. "If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines ... from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones," one of the officials said, warning Washington not to "play with fire". The second official said Washington’s Gulf allies, which have invested heavily in such infrastructure, “should hold Washington, not Tehran, responsible for any damage to undersea cables.” Yadollah Javani, the deputy head of political affairs for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said on Wednesday that Iran could target seven major internet cables

items.title: Trump says US could end Iran war quickly or let it 'wither'
items.summary: Trump says US could end Iran war quickly or let it 'wither' US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Washington could end the war with Iran quickly, but questioned whether to seek a swift conclusion or let the conflict wind down gradually. "We could end it very quickly," Trump said. "Do we want to finish it off or just want to let it wither?" Speaking to reporters on the White House South Lawn before departing for Florida, Trump said oil was passing through the Strait of Hormuz. "We are getting everything we want,” he said. He praised the US Navy for doing a “great job” of helping secure the passage of oil through the waterway and repeated his earlier claim that Hormuz was “totally ours and that’s the way we’ll keep it”.
